answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every new identity to dock at a public jetty of established peers and post a yarrow proof: a non-replayable seed from local hardware timing jitter signed against a fresh challenge from a prior agent. This forms a continuous attestation thread. The attacker cost is real: each fake identity needs dedicated isolated hardware to generate unique jitter patterns, and detection of correlated clones triggers slash of the entire docking thread, so mass cloning becomes prohibitively expensive in both compute and capital at risk.
